Only methods declared in sugar-charts/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

BarChart final class

Vertical bar chart. Mirrors ntcharts' barchart package — bars drawn with █ blocks. Bars are spaced one column apart and labels are written underneath, truncated to fit when too long. Y-axis range is computed from the data unless explicit withMin() / withMax() are provided.

MethodSummary
static new(iterable $bars = [], int $width = 40, int $height = 8): selfConstruct from either an array of [label, value] tuples, an array keyed label => value, or a list of Bar instances.
withBars(iterable $bars): self
push(Bar|array $bar): selfAppend a single bar to the chart. Accepts a Bar instance, a [label, value] tuple, or a label => value pair (when called via push(['Apple', 12]) or push(new Bar('Apple', 12))). Mirrors ntcharts' BarChart::Push(BarData). Immutable.
pushAll(iterable $bars): selfAppend every bar in $bars to the chart, in order. Accepts the same shapes as new(). Mirrors ntcharts' BarChart::PushAll.
clear(): selfDrop every bar. Mirrors ntcharts' Clear.
withSize(int $w, int $h): self
withMin(?float $m): self
withMax(?float $m): self
withShowLabels(bool $on): selfShow the CATEGORY labels under each bar (vertical) or left of each row (horizontal) — the axis text, not the values. For values on the bars use withDataLabels().
withHorizontal(bool $on = true): selfRender bars left-to-right instead of bottom-to-top. Each bar occupies one row and grows horizontally; the label sits in the leftmost column. Mirrors ntcharts' SetHorizontal.
withAxes(bool $on = true): selfDraw an axis line along the chart edge: vertical (┤) on the left in vertical mode, vertical (├) on the left of each bar row in horizontal mode. Canonical spelling shared with LineChart::withAxes() (sugar-charts-008 naming split converged here). Mirrors ntcharts' SetShowAxis.
withFractionalHeights(bool $on = true): selfRender the sub-cell remainder of each bar as an eighth-block cap instead of snapping the whole bar to full █ cells. Low-height charts otherwise make 0.9 and 0.51 indistinguishable once they round to the same cell count; the ramp keeps the residual visible while whole cells stay █ byte-for-byte as before. Vertical bars get a bottom-eighths cap (▁…▇) on the partial top row; horizontal bars get a left-flush cap (▏…▉) so the fill stays contiguous with the █ body — a right-flush glyph would open a gap at the cap. Residuals rounding to 0/8 eighths render blank/full respectively (no ▁ ghost from float noise). Default off — legacy output is preserved for existing consumers. Concept ported from the eighth-block ramp used by sugar-dashboard RenderBar.
withBarWidth(?int $width): selfPin every bar to a fixed cell width. Default null means "distribute available width across bars" (the prior behavior). Mirrors ntcharts' WithBarWidth. null re-enables auto.
withBarGap(?int $gap): selfPin the gap between bars. Default null means "1-cell gap when width allows". 0 packs bars edge-to-edge. null re-enables the auto gap (same explicit-null sentinel as withBarWidth()). Mirrors ntcharts' WithBarGap.
withNoAutoBarWidth(bool $on = true): selfDisable auto-fit of bar width (vertical mode; horizontal bars grow across the width and never auto-fit). With a pinned withBarWidth() this is equivalent to that pin alone; without one, each bar renders exactly 1 cell wide instead of distributing the available width — the ntcharts WithNoAutoBarWidth shape. false re-enables auto-fit and clears any width pin.
withBarColor(?\Closure $fn): selfPer-bar color resolver: fn(Bar $bar, int $i): ?Color, $i being the bar's index in $bars. A returned Color paints that bar's █ body and eighth-block cap; null leaves the bar unstyled. Gaps, labels and the axis are never colored. WHY: a single-color bar set cannot express per-bar heat (btop tints each meter by its value through the theme gradient). Mirrors btop's per-value Theme::g(...).at(value) lookup (btop_draw.cpp Meter::operator()).
supportsDataLabels(): boolRenderers that answer false refuse withDataLabels(true) (sugar-charts-024).
supportsAnimation(): boolNo progress-driven frame path exists on this renderer.
withDataLabels(bool $show = true): selfRender each bar's VALUE as a text label: a centered row above the bars (vertical mode, one cell-run per bar column) or a suffix trailing each row's bar (horizontal mode, only where the width budget fits). The category labels under the bars are the separate showLabels axis. Labels are plain text (never colored). Mirrors ntcharts' SetShowDataLabels.
withDataLabelFormatter(?\Closure $formatter = null): selfCustom value formatter: fn(Bar $bar, int $index): string. Default prints integral values bare and trims trailing zeros of a 2-decimal rendering (12 → "12", 2.5 → "2.5", 2.25 → "2.25").
withLegend(bool $show = true): selfToggle the legend. When switched on with no explicit items, one entry per bar is derived (bar label + palette color by index) so the switch is never a silent no-op.
withLegendPosition(Position $position): selfSet the legend position.
withLegendIndicator(?string $indicatorChar = null): selfCustomize the legend indicator glyph (one cell-wide rune). Passing null clears it back to the default bullet.
withTitle(?string $title = null, Position $position = Position::Top): selfSet the chart title.
withTitlePosition(Position $position): selfSet the title position separately.
withXLabel(?string $label = null): selfSet the X-axis label (rendered at bottom).
withYLabel(?string $label = null): selfSet the Y-axis label (prepended to each line).
withLegendItems(array $items): selfSet legend items directly (label + color pairs).

SugarCraft\Charts\Buffer

BufferHelper final class

Helpers for building Buffer-backed chart renderers.

MethodSummary
static graphemeWidth(string $cluster): intCompute the display width of a single grapheme cluster in terminal cells. Delegates to the shared sugar-core width table (Width::of()) so East-Asian, emoji (including plane-1), and combining marks follow the same canon as every other SugarCraft renderer — the old private table omitted plane-1 emoji despite its docblock claiming otherwise.
static clusters(string $s): arraySplit a string into display clusters — the fleet-proven ladder (identical to sugar-cellbuffer's Buffer::clusters): optional grapheme_str_split() accelerator (symfony polyfill / future core), then IntlBreakIterator character boundaries, which is what this package's hard ext-intl requirement guarantees (sugar-charts-044: without it combining marks and ZW sequences used to silently degrade to CODEPOINT cells — same bytes diverging per platform, zero diagnostic). The mb/preg codepoint arms remain only as defence for malformed UTF-8 and installs that bypass composer. Centralised here so the Buffer and Canvas placement paths cannot drift.
static clusterMode(): stringIntrospection seam for the splitter actually in force: 'grapheme' when either accelerator is available (composer contract via ext-intl) or 'codepoint' on a host that somehow lacks both arms. Diagnostics and tests pin which canon produced a render instead of guessing from platform bytes (sugar-charts-044).
static toBufferStyle(SugarStyle $s): BufferStyleConvert a sugar-style Style (SugarCraft\Style\Style) to a Buffer\Style. Only fg/bg/attrs are transferred; advanced features (borders, padding, etc.) are dropped.

Canvas final class

Fixed-size 2D grid of Cells. Charts draw onto the canvas and call view() to produce a ready-to-print frame. Coordinates are 0-based: $x is column, $y is row, with (0, 0) at the top-left.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly int $width, public readonly int $height)
width(): int
height(): int
setCell(int $x, int $y, string $rune, ?Style $style = null): voidWrite a single rune into cell ($x, $y). Out-of-range coordinates are silently dropped (no exception).
cell(int $x, int $y): CellRead the Cell at ($x, $y). Out-of-range coordinates return an empty placeholder Cell.
setCellStyle(int $x, int $y, ?Style $style): voidReplace a cell's style without changing its rune. Mirrors ntcharts' SetCellStyle. Out-of-range coordinates are no-ops.
cellStyle(int $x, int $y): ?StyleRead a cell's style (or null when unset). Mirrors ntcharts' GetCellStyle.
setRunes(int $x, int $y, iterable $runes, ?Style $style = null): voidPlace a horizontal run of $cells cells starting at ($x, $y), each carrying $rune (and optional shared $style). Mirrors ntcharts' SetRunes when used per-row. Cells that fall outside the canvas bounds are silently dropped.
setString(int $x, int $y, string $s, ?Style $style = null): voidPlace a string of glyphs along row $y starting at column $x. Split into display clusters via BufferHelper::clusters() (ICU grapheme boundaries through the hard ext-intl requirement; codepoint arms only guard malformed input). Mirrors ntcharts' SetString.
setLines(int $x, int $y, iterable $lines, ?Style $style = null): voidPlace pre-styled lines at ($x, $y) — each line goes on its own row. Mirrors ntcharts' SetLines. Each line is split through setString() so the same multibyte handling applies.
fill(int $x0, int $y0, int $x1, int $y1, string $rune, ?Style $style = null): voidFill every cell in the rectangle ($x0..$x1, $y0..$y1) (inclusive) with $rune (and optional $style). Out-of-range coordinates are clamped. Mirrors ntcharts' Fill.
fillLine(int $y, string $rune, ?Style $style = null): voidFill an entire row with $rune. Mirrors ntcharts' FillLine. Out-of-range rows are silently ignored.
shiftDown(int $n = 1): voidShift every cell down by $n rows. Cells that fall off the bottom are dropped; new rows at the top fill with empty cells. Mirrors ntcharts' ShiftDown.
shiftUp(int $n = 1): voidShift every cell up by $n rows. Mirrors ntcharts' ShiftUp. The bottom rows fill with empty cells.
shiftLeft(int $n = 1): voidShift every row left by $n columns. Cells that fall off the left are dropped; the right edge fills with empty cells. Mirrors ntcharts' ShiftLeft.
shiftRight(int $n = 1): voidShift every row right by $n columns. Cells that fall off the right are dropped; the left edge fills with empty cells. Mirrors ntcharts' ShiftRight.
clear(): voidReset every cell to empty. Mirrors ntcharts' Clear.
view(): stringRender the canvas as a string. Empty cells render as spaces; each row is right-trimmed, and rows join with "\n". Adjacent cells that share a style emit its escape sequence once for the whole run, and exactly one reset closes each styled run — the frame carries no per-cell reset spam.
viewPadded(): stringRender the canvas with every row padded to its full width — trailing cells (including a styled cell whose rune is a space) survive. Overlay hosts that blit the frame onto an existing screen need the full rectangle; view() trims it away.

Braille dot-matrix mode is selected by withBraille(), independently of the grid choice — the two compose: a braille raster can be painted into any grid.

The theme's palette drives every series color and legend indicator: series render in primary/accent/info/success/warning/secondary/error order (cycling), and the legend recolors to match. Without a theme, series render with their default colors (cell mode: unstyled; braille mode: the legend's CSS colors) — the unthemed output is byte-identical. Honored by LineChart, the only class extending this base; BarChart and the rest compose their own legends via the ChartExtras trait and have no theme surface. Use Theme::dracula(), Theme::oneDark(), etc. Mirrors sugar-style Theme palette roles.

SugarCraft\Charts\LineChart

LineChart final class

Multi-series line plot drawn onto a Canvas. Each data point becomes one column; the series is scaled into the canvas height and a * (configurable) is plotted at the rounded row. Adjacent points are connected with |, /, or \ strokes when their rows differ, giving an at-a-glance trend without requiring sub-cell rasterization. The unnamed $data series renders first; withDataset() adds named series on the same Y scale with automatic legend entries and a cycling per-series color. withTheme() recolors every series and legend indicator from a sugar-style Theme palette, and withUnicodeConnectors() swaps the connector strokes for the │ ─ ╱ ╲ runes used by Waveline (ASCII remains the default).

OHLCChart final class

OHLC / candlestick chart drawn onto a Canvas. Each bar gets one column: a vertical wick spanning low → high, with a thicker body covering open ↔ close. Bullish bars (close > open) and bearish bars (close < open) use distinct glyphs and colors so the direction of motion is obvious at a glance. Doji bars (open == close, a no-change period) carry their own glyph and color arm (sugar-charts-101) instead of silently bearing the bearish body.

Documented semantic change: after the window fills, the oldest bar is dropped at push time rather than at render time. Growing $width later cannot resurrect dropped bars; withBars() is the full-replace door.

SugarCraft\Charts\Picture

Picture final class

Inline-image renderer for SugarCharts. Accepts a 2D RGB pixel grid and emits the appropriate terminal escape sequence for the active (or explicitly-selected) image protocol.

MethodSummary
static fromGrid(array $pixels): self
static fromPng(string $pngBytes): selfBuild from pre-encoded PNG bytes — caller produces these via imagepng() (ext-gd) or Imagick. Required for the Kitty / iTerm2 protocols since both wrap base64'd PNG.
withProtocol(?Protocol $p): self
withPaletteSize(int $n): self
protocol(?Protocol $p): selfShort-form alias for withProtocol().
paletteSize(int $n): selfShort-form alias for withPaletteSize().
static detect(?array $env = null): ?ProtocolPick a protocol based on the running terminal's capabilities. Honours $TERM_PROGRAM (iTerm2, WezTerm), $TERM (kitty, foot, mlterm), $KITTY_WINDOW_ID, and the Windows Terminal pair $WT_SESSION/$WT_PROFILE_ID.
intrinsicSize(): arrayHonest image frame size [w, h] in PIXELS (sugar-charts-010).
view(): string
__toString(): string

Protocol enum

Inline-image escape protocol used by Picture. Mirrors the escape routing of ntcharts' picture module; the Protocol enum abstraction itself is lib-local. Each protocol encodes pixel data into a different escape envelope:

Cases: Sixel · Kitty · ITerm2

PHP also provides cases(), from() and tryFrom().

Sixel final class

Pure-PHP Sixel encoder (antecedent: the Sixel DCS grammar, ISO 8613-6; serves ntcharts' picture Sixel-fallback role — the encoder implementation is lib-local). Translates a 2D RGB pixel grid into a ESC P q ... ESC \ Device Control String suitable for terminals that speak Sixel. Wire support: xterm (only --enable-sixel builds), mlterm, foot, iTerm2, WezTerm, Windows Terminal (preview-gated since 1.18). Picture::detect() auto-routes mlterm/foot/WezTerm/Windows Terminal (plus iTerm2/kitty to their native protocols); bare xterm has no reliable env signal and needs an explicit withProtocol().

MethodSummary
static encode(array $pixels, int $paletteSize = 16): stringEncode $pixels (a [row][col] => Color grid) into a Sixel escape sequence.

SugarCraft\Charts\Sparkline

Sparkline final class

Compact single-row chart drawn with the eight Unicode block-bar glyphs ▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█. Each data point becomes one cell whose height is proportional to the value within [min, max].

MethodSummary
static new(array $data = [], int $width = -1): selfConstruct a sparkline. $width = -1 (the default) auto-fits the width to the number of data points; pass an explicit 0 to render nothing. Any other negative throws — one sentinel rule shared with withWidth() (sugar-charts-104).
withData(array $data): self
withWidth(int $w): self
withMin(?float $m): self
withMax(?float $m): self
withStyle(?Style $style): selfStyle applied to every glyph in view(). Pass null to render unstyled. Mirrors ntcharts' WithStyle.
data(?array $data = null): array|self
width(?int $w = null): int|self
min(?float $m = null): float|self|null
max(?float $m = null): float|self|null
style(?Style $style): selfShort-form alias for withStyle().
push(int|float $value): selfAppend a single sample. Mirrors ntcharts' Sparkline::Push(value). The window slide in view() keeps only the last width points, so callers can append indefinitely without trimming.
pushAll(array $values): selfAppend every sample in $values, in order. Mirrors ntcharts' Sparkline::PushAll([]float64).
clear(): selfDrop every recorded sample. Mirrors ntcharts' Clear.
intrinsicSize(): arrayHonest rendered-frame size [w, h] of view() (sugar-charts-010).
view(): string
cells(): arrayThe per-cell runes of the rendered row — one entry per display column (empty string for a blank or a wide-glyph continuation), which makes implode('', $sparkline->cells()) equal to Ansi::strip($sparkline->view()) on every host. The structured sibling of view() for consumers that need cells, not bytes: re-parsing the ANSI output with preg_split becomes unnecessary (sugar-charts-027).
__toString(): string

SugarCraft\Charts\Support

CellGrid interface

The write-side contract of a character cell grid: the surface renderers paint into, declared so withCanvas() can accept any grid implementation (sugar-charts-007 — sugar-charts' own Canvas, a test double, or a host application's grid) instead of being an inert mode flag.

MethodSummary
setCell(int $x, int $y, string $rune, ?Style $style = null): voidPaint one cell. A rune wider than one cell is the canvas's call — Canvas collapses it to a single cell per its documented clamp.
setString(int $x, int $y, string $text, ?Style $style = null): voidPaint a string horizontally from ($x, $y), one grapheme cluster per cell, advancing by each cluster's display width.
width(): intThe canvas width in cells. Charts consult it when they size a render into a foreign grid.
height(): intThe canvas height in cells.
view(): stringThe rendered view: rows joined by newlines, exactly as a chart's view() would emit.

ColorLadder final class

The NO_COLOR / CLICOLOR decision ladder, shared by every emitter.

MethodSummary
static suppressed(): bool
static guard(string $output): stringLadder-adjust a composed render: byte-identical passthrough when color is allowed, SGR-free text when suppressed.
static stripSgr(string $output): stringRemove the SGR family (CSI … m) from any string — the mechanism self::guard() applies when the ladder says "suppressed"; exposed so the parity test can name the exact removed set.
static carriesSgr(string $output): boolTrue when $output carries any SGR sequence — the matrix test's discriminator (color emitted at all).

Range final class

Range-pin ingestion guard shared by every axis-range setter.

MethodSummary
static pin(?float $min, ?float $max, string $axis): voidAssert one axis pair is a legal explicit range.
static resolve(?float $pinMin, ?float $pinMax, float $scanMin, float $scanMax, string $axis): arrayCombine pinned ends with the scanned data extents BEFORE anything normalizes by (max − min) (sugar-charts-056). A lone pinned end is legal at the door, but if the resolved pair comes out inverted — e.g. a pinned min above every sample — the old silent clamp drew all-zero bars, flat candles, and a misleading steady mid-glyph. Fail loudly instead: the chart refuses to render a domain that cannot contain its own data.

Rune final class

Single-cell ingress door for runes the renderers paint one cell at a time (point glyphs, scatter/heatmap fills, candle bodies/wicks, legend indicators).

MethodSummary
static cell(string $rune, string $name): stringGuard $rune and assert the result is exactly one display cell.

UntrustedText final class

Trust boundary for every string this library can echo to a terminal.

MethodSummary
static guard(string $value): stringMake $value safe to render inside a fixed-width chart frame.
static guardItems(array $items): arrayGuard every label entry of a legend-item shaped list (list<array{label: string, color: string}>). Colors are validated separately at render time; only the human-readable text needs the sweep.
